name: The Nasty Bits: Sautéed Duck Livers with Rhubarb and Cherry Sauce

ingredients.name: A few tablespoons cornstarch, for coating the livers
dark red cherries, either Bing or another variety

instructions.primary_message: To make the sauce: Rinse the cherries and rhubarb in cold water. Chop the stalks of rhubarb into 0.5-cm slices. Remove the pits from the cherries and chop into halves. Place the rhubarb and the cherries in a small saucepan, along with the sugar. Simmer over low heat for 20 minutes. The sauce should be like compote: fleshy and soft, with a few pieces of cherry still intact. Depending on the tartness of your cherries, you may need to add a bit more sugar. If desired, add a splash of vinegar at the end. The sauce may be made in advance and set aside.
Dry your livers on a towel; then cut them up into 2.5-cm segments and set aside.

schema_metadata.keywords: duck, duck liver, liver, offal, poultry, rhubarb, The Nasty Bits

description: If you've only experienced the creaminess of chicken liver, try to imagine the indulgence of duck liver. Its texture, though a far cry from foie gras, approaches the richness of something that tastes too good to be a humble cut of offal sold for a pittance.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 1 teaspoon fig balsamic vinegar, optional

Optional substitutions: A few tablespoons cornstarch → flour; butter → duck fat
author: Chichi Wang
